clue.text: Spoke about Conservative one who favours extreme change

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for spoke surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: a spoke of a wheel is a radial

explanation.surface: A political commentator talks about the Tory party and a would-be reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like a past tense verb but is the noun: a wheel spoke, RADIAL, wrapped 'about' C.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical is a person who wants sweeping, root-and-branch reform of society or politics.

clue.text: Starts to renovate old cottage of church officer in an old decorative style

indicators.note: the starts of a run of words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A church officer's old cottage is to be done up in a period style.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century style of curves, scrolls and shell motifs in architecture and furniture.

clue.text: Reserved object, last in sale

parts.note: to object is to demur, raise a protest

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter, here of sale

explanation.surface: A shy bidder raises an objection to the final lot at an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' could be a reserve price at the sale, but it is the definition; 'object' is a verb, not a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a modest, quiet, retiring manner, particularly in a young woman.

clue.text: Drag a scout free — this rescue worker might

indicators.note: setting the letters free lets them fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who pulls a stranded Boy Scout clear of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a whole: such a rescuer might indeed drag a scout free.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastguards are the service that watches the shore and rescues people in trouble at sea.

clue.text: American after fortune for plant

indicators.note: after places the American abbreviation behind the word for fortune

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or destiny
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: An American chasing his fortune with a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, an aquatic flowering plant sacred in Asian religions.

clue.text: Framework of church when applied to sister

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A church's structural framework, applied to a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a car or other vehicle on which the body is built.

clue.text: Cold fish on shoot gets a wrap?

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on a tap
the ling is a long fish of the cod family
to shoot a scene is to film it

explanation.surface: Chilled fish on a photo shoot gets wrapped up, like a film finishing production.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts one piece below another. 'Wrap' is also what a director says to end a shoot, a nod to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cling film is thin transparent plastic used to cover and wrap food, so it is an example of a wrap.

clue.text: Article about a neighbourhood

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerning a local district.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a district or region, the stretch of town around where one lives.

clue.text: Deposit small sum of money in crumpled tens

indicators.note: in puts the coin inside the rearranged letters
crumpled notes are twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a dime is a ten-cent coin, a trifling sum

explanation.surface: Banking a few cents among some crumpled ten-pound notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like a banking verb paired with the money, but it is the noun definition; 'crumpled' rearranges TENS to SENT around the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles and is laid down at the bottom of a liquid, a deposit.

clue.text: Bolt, maybe, in small piece of office equipment

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a printer is a standard office machine

explanation.surface: A bolt or screw found in a little office machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like hardware; it is Usain Bolt, the Jamaican athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Usain Bolt holds the 100 m world record, an example of a fast runner over short races.

clue.text: Usual? Not on a butterfly

indicators.note: not on says the two letters of on are left out

parts.note: usual and common both mean ordinary, everyday

explanation.surface: Is it normal? No, not on a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The comma is a European butterfly named for the white comma-shaped mark under its wing.

clue.text: One of the last to go in, kind welcoming trouble

definitions.text: One of the last to go in

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the word for kind holds the other

parts.note: tender means gentle and kind
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A kindly host welcoming a troubled guest, among the last to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, batsmen 'go in' to bat in order; the weakest batsmen come in last.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender is a poor batsman placed at the bottom of a cricket batting order.

clue.text: Copper gets gear changed, some of it good, some of it bad

definitions.text: some of it good, some of it bad

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman shifts gear, sometimes well, sometimes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the element. The phrase comes from a Punch cartoon in which a nervous young clergyman says his bad egg is 'good in parts'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names something of mixed quality, partly good and partly bad, after the cartoon's polite clergyman.

clue.text: Ordinary guys writing on the wall

parts.note: O stands for ordinary, as in the old O level exams
guys are men

explanation.surface: Everyday blokes scrawling graffiti.
explanation.walkthrough: The writing on the wall is the Biblical warning at Belshazzar's feast.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing on the wall is an idiom for a sign of coming disaster, a portent.

clue.text: Golf course in narrow valley — good scores there

parts.note: a glen is a narrow Scottish valley
on a golf course an eagle is two under par, a good score

explanation.surface: A golf course in a glen where players score well.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleneagles is a famous golf resort in Perthshire, Scotland, which hosted the 2014 Ryder Cup.

clue.text: CCTV, perhaps, almost always effective — conceal weapon

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a sure remedy is one that always works
to veil is to hide or conceal
a lance is a long spear carried by knights

explanation.surface: A closed-circuit camera that nearly always works, concealing a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: CCTV cameras watch over public places, an example of close monitoring of people.

clue.text: Winner, Scotsman, becoming strait-laced

parts.note: a victor is a winner
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scottish champion turns prudish.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective evokes the prim, moralistic attitudes associated with the reign of Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Huge company deficit a line shows

parts.note: a loss is a deficit

explanation.surface: A firm's accounts reveal an enormous shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size, like the Colossus of Rhodes.

clue.text: Protest about renegade party member

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
c, for circa, means about
a rat is someone who deserts or betrays a cause

explanation.surface: Demonstrating against a turncoat from the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to the Democratic Party, one of the two big US political parties.

clue.text: Obsession of individual recording soul

parts.note: one means a single individual
a track is a recording on an album
mind and soul both mean the inner self

explanation.surface: One person's fixation with soul music records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soul' suggests the music genre; here it is the inner self.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes thinking constantly about one thing, a fixation.

clue.text: Stretch of lake twists to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north means read from bottom to top

parts.note: L stands for lake on maps
warps means twists or bends out of shape

explanation.surface: A long reach of lake winding northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to stretch out one's limbs loosely, or spread out untidily.

clue.text: Morse creator put off about vote

indicators.note: about means around, so the verb surrounds the voting mark

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Samuel Morse, inventor of the code, discouraged from voting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse' suggests the telegraph code, but it is Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of books and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin Dexter wrote the novels featuring Inspector Morse, so he is that character's creator.

clue.text: Honour holding old musical instrument

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the award goes round the letter

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A decorated veteran with an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument in the orchestra.

clue.text: On account of test, short prayer required, say

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in 'jailed for theft'
an exam is a test

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request, a prayer

explanation.surface: Because of an exam, a quick prayer is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Say is used to introduce an instance, as in 'pick a number, say seven'.

clue.text: Keen listener comprehending good English

indicators.note: comprehending means including within, so the organ surrounds the two letters

parts.note: the ear is the organ one listens with

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic listener who understands decent English.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean enthusiastic, wanting to do something.

clue.text: Real solid houses to boot

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the letters are sitting inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Genuinely solid houses, and more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' is not footwear: 'to boot' means in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning as well, in addition.

clue.text: Sauntering in street, swaggering

parts.note: a rolling gait is a swaying, swaggering walk

explanation.surface: Someone ambling down the road with a swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe walking slowly and leisurely, without hurry.

clue.text: Lowest score, ultimately, in final

indicators.note: in places the end letter inside the word for final

parts.note: last means final

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: The bottom score at the end of a cup final.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means smallest in amount or rank, the lowest.

clue.text: Lengthen lease, in writing

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it
down means recorded on paper, as in 'get it down'

explanation.surface: Extending a tenancy agreement on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To let down a hem or a garment is to make it longer by releasing the turned-up fabric.

clue.text: Slammer, finally — bad result for cattle thief

indicators.note: finally points to the end letter of the word before it
bad means corrupt or spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prison at last, a bad outcome for a cattle thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals livestock, especially cattle or horses, in the Wild West.
